name: Make Refine upgrades a one-click agent-managed operation

current_round.prompt:
Implement a one-click, agent-managed Refine source upgrade that removes workflow-state decisions from the user. Ground the implementation in the existing Controls > Node > Refine (dev) Upgrade capability and reuse its shared source inspection, candidate build, restart-safe handoff, service-registration replacement, live executable identity verification, rollback, durable operation state, API, SSE, and reconnect behavior instead of creating a second updater.

Update discovery must be performant. Add one authoritative server-side cached update-check state with last-check time, current and available source identity, freshness, in-flight status, and actionable failure. Automatically refresh the remote at most once per hour by default, coalesce concurrent checks, and persist enough state across page refreshes and daemon restart. Do not run git fetch for every nav render, menu open, route change, SSE event, client poll, or reconnect. A manual check may request a fresh remote check, but duplicate clicks and concurrent clients must share one in-flight operation. Keep the cadence defined in one testable place and expose when the last successful check occurred.

In the web UI main navigation Controls menu, present one compact stateful control whenever the running Refine checkout/update channel is discoverable; do not gate the running Refine node's updater on whether the currently attached target app is itself Refine. When no update is known, the cached result is stale, or Refine is current, the control offers Check for updates and shows checking, current, stale, or error feedback as appropriate. When a newer fetched revision is available, the same control becomes an enabled Upgrade Refine button and identifies the available update without requiring the user to visit Refine (dev). During orchestration it shows durable progress, reconnecting, success, failure, and retry states. Preserve keyboard and screen-reader behavior. One click on Upgrade Refine is the authorization to begin; do not add a second confirmation dialog.

Clicking Upgrade Refine must launch exactly one dedicated managed upgrade Agent and return a durable operation receipt. The Agent owns the end-to-end maintenance plan and delegates privileged Git, process, installation, lifecycle, and source-promotion mutations through shared typed Refine capabilities rather than inventing browser-side shell commands. The operation must be idempotent across repeated clicks, browser closure, daemon termination, and restart, and must not consume a normal Goal workflow claim or deadlock by counting its own Agent or restart-safe handoff as upgrade-blocking active work.

Make workflow state an orchestration input rather than an affordance blocker. The Agent records the pre-upgrade pause/admission state, pauses new workflow claims when needed, observes active Goal agents, Quality, merge, build, terminal, and managed processes, and drains, checkpoints, or safely reconciles them before promotion. It must work when automation begins running, already paused, idle, or carrying active work. Preserve Goal records, claims, worktrees, branches, review boundaries, logs, and recoverable process state; never discard dirty work, force Git history, hide a failure, or report success from checkout HEAD alone. If a non-workflow source condition such as dirty or diverged controller source cannot be resolved safely and non-destructively, retain the checkout untouched and surface precise recovery evidence rather than forcing it.

Once safe, fetch and fast-forward the configured Refine source, build the candidate before stopping the live daemon, then use the existing restart-safe source-promotion and port-scoped service lifecycle machinery to activate and restart it. Prove success from the live daemon's candidate executable identity and health. On activation, registration, restart, reachability, or identity failure, use the existing authoritative rollback behavior and retain partial or unknown evidence plus actionable recovery; never claim the system is online while the wrong executable is running.

After restart, reconcile the same durable upgrade operation, restore the user's prior workflow admission intent rather than blindly resuming an intentionally paused workflow, recover or reconnect preserved workflow work and required managed infrastructure, and verify the Refine daemon, runner, attached target-app lifecycle, and UI event stream are online. The browser must automatically reconnect and settle the nav control from authoritative operation state. A completed update refreshes the cached source identity; a failed or interrupted update remains visible and safely retryable.

Add proportionate deterministic and integration coverage for the hourly cache and manual refresh, request coalescing, current and available UI states, target-app-independent visibility, one-click Agent launch, idempotency, initially running and initially paused workflows, active claims and managed processes, no self-deadlock, browser disconnect and daemon restart reconciliation, preservation and exact pause-state restoration, dirty and diverged source protection, candidate identity success, rollback and indeterminate failure evidence, and multi-client retries. Extend the existing source-promotion, lifecycle, API, SSE, static/browser, and real installed-service tests where appropriate. Update the affected System/API/browser intent, Rust spec, and upgrade runbook so the manual Refine (dev) screen and the new Agent-orchestrated main-nav path have one shared authority and clearly documented recovery semantics. Leave the Goal in the normal reviewable workflow; do not auto-approve or merge it.

governance.constitution:
- Organize Refine as Foundation, Capabilities, and Surfaces. Foundation holds the durable concepts, Capabilities own the powers and product semantics, and Surfaces remain replaceable adapters.
- Keep the foundation small and legible: Nodes, Goals, Features, target-app context, workflow state, settings, and evidence must remain explicit enough for people and agents to inspect.
- Keep Process, Agents, and Workflow as shared capabilities. They may evolve or be replaced, but their responsibilities and composition must remain coherent across the system.
- Preserve local ownership. Authoritative state, Git history, settings, runtime records, and agent output must be inspectable and recoverable; caches and projections must remain derived.
- Be agent-first by using installed coding-agent CLIs and host tools through shared configuration, process supervision, workflow, and evidence rather than provider- or surface-specific product paths.
- Treat workflow as durable state advancement, process as the observable execution substrate, and agents as actors that use both without redefining either.
- Prefer mitigation and accountability over broad capability denial: isolation, Git, governance, quality, review, visible errors, and recovery should make powerful work safe enough to use.
- Preserve room for architectural discovery. A better design may replace current machinery when it explains the tradeoff, protects product intent, and supplies proportionate migration and verification evidence.
governance.product: Refine is a local-first, agent-first operating layer for software delivery. It turns understandable Goals and Features into reviewable changes by coordinating explicit workflow state, supervised processes, installed coding-agent CLIs, Git isolation, quality, governance, and durable evidence across one or many Nodes. Its core promise is that powerful autonomous work remains user-owned, inspectable, recoverable, and consistent across replaceable human and agent surfaces.

rules.text: Respect the Foundation-Capabilities-Surfaces boundary: durable concepts belong in the model and target-app foundation, product behavior and orchestration belong in shared capabilities, and UI, CLI, API, desktop, and agent surfaces stay thin and semantically consistent.

Compose the existing Process, Agents, Workflow, Git, state, quality, governance, and evidence capabilities before creating new machinery. Each concern should have one authoritative implementation and source of truth unless the Goal explicitly proposes an architectural replacement.

Keep authoritative target-app state local, durable, inspectable, and outside the primary source worktree; keep runtime artifacts separate and projections or caches rebuildable. State-layout changes require a compatible migration or explicit transition plan.

Keep the daemon and surfaces responsive by running agent, Git, quality, lifecycle, and other long-running work through the supervised process substrate with explicit ownership, status, logs, cancellation, failure feedback, and recovery.

Coordinate parallel or distributed work explicitly through Node ownership, workflow claims and capacity, dependency or Feature ordering, and isolated Git branches or worktrees so concurrent changes remain reviewable and recoverable.

Require evidence proportional to actual architectural and operational risk. Verify the affected behavior with the smallest focused checks that provide confidence, including integration or failure-path evidence when a change alters concurrency, persistence, process, Git, release, recovery, or cross-surface semantics. Update only affected docs/intent pages when documented product intent or an architectural contract changes; do not require unrelated documentation or broad cleanup.

Allow architectural evolution when a Goal states the protected product intent, explains why the new design is better, updates capability boundaries and intent docs, and provides migration, compatibility, and verification evidence proportionate to the change.

Keep Refine agent-first: delegate adaptable reasoning and execution to installed agents through shared context and tools instead of duplicating it in bespoke product logic or surface-specific controls. Add first-class functionality when it provides durable coordination, state, synchronization, supervision, evidence, recovery, accessibility, deterministic integrity, or a materially better shared human and agent surface; preserve one capability across UI, CLI, API, and MCP.

Use SSE as the only mechanism for live browser updates. UI code must not use periodic polling, retry loops, timers, or repeated status GETs to observe background work or state changes; use one-shot authoritative reads only for initial load, operation registration race closure, reconnect reconciliation, or explicit user refresh.

previous_rounds.prompt:
Implement a one-click, agent-managed Refine source upgrade that removes workflow-state decisions from the user. Ground the implementation in the existing Controls > Node > Refine (dev) Upgrade capability and reuse its shared source inspection, candidate build, restart-safe handoff, service-registration replacement, live executable identity verification, rollback, durable operation state, API, SSE, and reconnect behavior instead of creating a second updater.

Update discovery must be performant. Add one authoritative server-side cached update-check state with last-check time, current and available source identity, freshness, in-flight status, and actionable failure. Automatically refresh the remote at most once per hour by default, coalesce concurrent checks, and persist enough state across page refreshes and daemon restart. Do not run git fetch for every nav render, menu open, route change, SSE event, client poll, or reconnect. A manual check may request a fresh remote check, but duplicate clicks and concurrent clients must share one in-flight operation. Keep the cadence defined in one testable place and expose when the last successful check occurred.

In the web UI main navigation Controls menu, present one compact stateful control whenever the running Refine checkout/update channel is discoverable; do not gate the running Refine node's updater on whether the currently attached target app is itself Refine. When no update is known, the cached result is stale, or Refine is current, the control offers Check for updates and shows checking, current, stale, or error feedback as appropriate. When a newer fetched revision is available, the same control becomes an enabled Upgrade Refine button and identifies the available update without requiring the user to visit Refine (dev). During orchestration it shows durable progress, reconnecting, success, failure, and retry states. Preserve keyboard and screen-reader behavior. One click on Upgrade Refine is the authorization to begin; do not add a second confirmation dialog.

Clicking Upgrade Refine must launch exactly one dedicated managed upgrade Agent and return a durable operation receipt. The Agent owns the end-to-end maintenance plan and delegates privileged Git, process, installation, lifecycle, and source-promotion mutations through shared typed Refine capabilities rather than inventing browser-side shell commands. The operation must be idempotent across repeated clicks, browser closure, daemon termination, and restart, and must not consume a normal Goal workflow claim or deadlock by counting its own Agent or restart-safe handoff as upgrade-blocking active work.

Make workflow state an orchestration input rather than an affordance blocker. The Agent records the pre-upgrade pause/admission state, pauses new workflow claims when needed, observes active Goal agents, Quality, merge, build, terminal, and managed processes, and drains, checkpoints, or safely reconciles them before promotion. It must work when automation begins running, already paused, idle, or carrying active work. Preserve Goal records, claims, worktrees, branches, review boundaries, logs, and recoverable process state; never discard dirty work, force Git history, hide a failure, or report success from checkout HEAD alone. If a non-workflow source condition such as dirty or diverged controller source cannot be resolved safely and non-destructively, retain the checkout untouched and surface precise recovery evidence rather than forcing it.

Once safe, fetch and fast-forward the configured Refine source, build the candidate before stopping the live daemon, then use the existing restart-safe source-promotion and port-scoped service lifecycle machinery to activate and restart it. Prove success from the live daemon's candidate executable identity and health. On activation, registration, restart, reachability, or identity failure, use the existing authoritative rollback behavior and retain partial or unknown evidence plus actionable recovery; never claim the system is online while the wrong executable is running.

After restart, reconcile the same durable upgrade operation, restore the user's prior workflow admission intent rather than blindly resuming an intentionally paused workflow, recover or reconnect preserved workflow work and required managed infrastructure, and verify the Refine daemon, runner, attached target-app lifecycle, and UI event stream are online. The browser must automatically reconnect and settle the nav control from authoritative operation state. A completed update refreshes the cached source identity; a failed or interrupted update remains visible and safely retryable.

Add proportionate deterministic and integration coverage for the hourly cache and manual refresh, request coalescing, current and available UI states, target-app-independent visibility, one-click Agent launch, idempotency, initially running and initially paused workflows, active claims and managed processes, no self-deadlock, browser disconnect and daemon restart reconciliation, preservation and exact pause-state restoration, dirty and diverged source protection, candidate identity success, rollback and indeterminate failure evidence, and multi-client retries. Extend the existing source-promotion, lifecycle, API, SSE, static/browser, and real installed-service tests where appropriate. Update the affected System/API/browser intent, Rust spec, and upgrade runbook so the manual Refine (dev) screen and the new Agent-orchestrated main-nav path have one shared authority and clearly documented recovery semantics. Leave the Goal in the normal reviewable workflow; do not auto-approve or merge it.

goal.name: Make Refine upgrades a one-click agent-managed operation

governance.constitution:
- Organize Refine as Foundation, Capabilities, and Surfaces. Foundation holds the durable concepts, Capabilities own the powers and product semantics, and Surfaces remain replaceable adapters.
- Keep the foundation small and legible: Nodes, Goals, Features, target-app context, workflow state, settings, and evidence must remain explicit enough for people and agents to inspect.
- Keep Process, Agents, and Workflow as shared capabilities. They may evolve or be replaced, but their responsibilities and composition must remain coherent across the system.
- Preserve local ownership. Authoritative state, Git history, settings, runtime records, and agent output must be inspectable and recoverable; caches and projections must remain derived.
- Be agent-first by using installed coding-agent CLIs and host tools through shared configuration, process supervision, workflow, and evidence rather than provider- or surface-specific product paths.
- Treat workflow as durable state advancement, process as the observable execution substrate, and agents as actors that use both without redefining either.
- Prefer mitigation and accountability over broad capability denial: isolation, Git, governance, quality, review, visible errors, and recovery should make powerful work safe enough to use.
- Preserve room for architectural discovery. A better design may replace current machinery when it explains the tradeoff, protects product intent, and supplies proportionate migration and verification evidence.
governance.product: Refine is a local-first, agent-first operating layer for software delivery. It turns understandable Goals and Features into reviewable changes by coordinating explicit workflow state, supervised processes, installed coding-agent CLIs, Git isolation, quality, governance, and durable evidence across one or many Nodes. Its core promise is that powerful autonomous work remains user-owned, inspectable, recoverable, and consistent across replaceable human and agent surfaces.

rules.text: Respect the Foundation-Capabilities-Surfaces boundary: durable concepts belong in the model and target-app foundation, product behavior and orchestration belong in shared capabilities, and UI, CLI, API, desktop, and agent surfaces stay thin and semantically consistent.

Compose the existing Process, Agents, Workflow, Git, state, quality, governance, and evidence capabilities before creating new machinery. Each concern should have one authoritative implementation and source of truth unless the Goal explicitly proposes an architectural replacement.

Keep authoritative target-app state local, durable, inspectable, and outside the primary source worktree; keep runtime artifacts separate and projections or caches rebuildable. State-layout changes require a compatible migration or explicit transition plan.

Keep the daemon and surfaces responsive by running agent, Git, quality, lifecycle, and other long-running work through the supervised process substrate with explicit ownership, status, logs, cancellation, failure feedback, and recovery.

Coordinate parallel or distributed work explicitly through Node ownership, workflow claims and capacity, dependency or Feature ordering, and isolated Git branches or worktrees so concurrent changes remain reviewable and recoverable.

Require evidence proportional to actual architectural and operational risk. Verify the affected behavior with the smallest focused checks that provide confidence, including integration or failure-path evidence when a change alters concurrency, persistence, process, Git, release, recovery, or cross-surface semantics. Update only affected docs/intent pages when documented product intent or an architectural contract changes; do not require unrelated documentation or broad cleanup.

Allow architectural evolution when a Goal states the protected product intent, explains why the new design is better, updates capability boundaries and intent docs, and provides migration, compatibility, and verification evidence proportionate to the change.

Keep Refine agent-first: delegate adaptable reasoning and execution to installed agents through shared context and tools instead of duplicating it in bespoke product logic or surface-specific controls. Add first-class functionality when it provides durable coordination, state, synchronization, supervision, evidence, recovery, accessibility, deterministic integrity, or a materially better shared human and agent surface; preserve one capability across UI, CLI, API, and MCP.

Use SSE as the only mechanism for live browser updates. UI code must not use periodic polling, retry loops, timers, or repeated status GETs to observe background work or state changes; use one-shot authoritative reads only for initial load, operation registration race closure, reconnect reconciliation, or explicit user refresh.

goal.name: Make Refine upgrades a one-click agent-managed operation

governance.constitution:
- Organize Refine as Foundation, Capabilities, and Surfaces. Foundation holds the durable concepts, Capabilities own the powers and product semantics, and Surfaces remain replaceable adapters.
- Keep the foundation small and legible: Nodes, Goals, Features, target-app context, workflow state, settings, and evidence must remain explicit enough for people and agents to inspect.
- Keep Process, Agents, and Workflow as shared capabilities. They may evolve or be replaced, but their responsibilities and composition must remain coherent across the system.
- Preserve local ownership. Authoritative state, Git history, settings, runtime records, and agent output must be inspectable and recoverable; caches and projections must remain derived.
- Be agent-first by using installed coding-agent CLIs and host tools through shared configuration, process supervision, workflow, and evidence rather than provider- or surface-specific product paths.
- Treat workflow as durable state advancement, process as the observable execution substrate, and agents as actors that use both without redefining either.
- Prefer mitigation and accountability over broad capability denial: isolation, Git, governance, quality, review, visible errors, and recovery should make powerful work safe enough to use.
- Preserve room for architectural discovery. A better design may replace current machinery when it explains the tradeoff, protects product intent, and supplies proportionate migration and verification evidence.
governance.product: Refine is a local-first, agent-first operating layer for software delivery. It turns understandable Goals and Features into reviewable changes by coordinating explicit workflow state, supervised processes, installed coding-agent CLIs, Git isolation, quality, governance, and durable evidence across one or many Nodes. Its core promise is that powerful autonomous work remains user-owned, inspectable, recoverable, and consistent across replaceable human and agent surfaces.

rules.text: Respect the Foundation-Capabilities-Surfaces boundary: durable concepts belong in the model and target-app foundation, product behavior and orchestration belong in shared capabilities, and UI, CLI, API, desktop, and agent surfaces stay thin and semantically consistent.

Compose the existing Process, Agents, Workflow, Git, state, quality, governance, and evidence capabilities before creating new machinery. Each concern should have one authoritative implementation and source of truth unless the Goal explicitly proposes an architectural replacement.

Keep authoritative target-app state local, durable, inspectable, and outside the primary source worktree; keep runtime artifacts separate and projections or caches rebuildable. State-layout changes require a compatible migration or explicit transition plan.

Run agents, Git, quality, lifecycle, and long work through the supervised process substrate, with explicit ownership, status, logs, cancellation, failures, and recovery. When activating a new Refine build requires replacing or restarting that supervisor, a restart-safe handoff may run outside it and independently complete the upgrade. The handoff must retain durable, operation-correlated ownership and state, visible progress and failures, and restart, rollback, and recovery reconciliation.

Coordinate parallel or distributed work explicitly through Node ownership, workflow claims and capacity, dependency or Feature ordering, and isolated Git branches or worktrees so concurrent changes remain reviewable and recoverable.

Require evidence proportional to actual architectural and operational risk. Verify the affected behavior with the smallest focused checks that provide confidence, including integration or failure-path evidence when a change alters concurrency, persistence, process, Git, release, recovery, or cross-surface semantics. Update only affected docs/intent pages when documented product intent or an architectural contract changes; do not require unrelated documentation or broad cleanup.

Allow architectural evolution when a Goal states the protected product intent, explains why the new design is better, updates capability boundaries and intent docs, and provides migration, compatibility, and verification evidence proportionate to the change.

Keep Refine agent-first: delegate adaptable reasoning and execution to installed agents through shared context and tools instead of duplicating it in bespoke product logic or surface-specific controls. Add first-class functionality when it provides durable coordination, state, synchronization, supervision, evidence, recovery, accessibility, deterministic integrity, or a materially better shared human and agent surface; preserve one capability across UI, CLI, API, and MCP.

Implement a one-click, agent-managed Refine source upgrade that removes workflow-state decisions from the user. Update discovery must be performant. Add one authoritative server-side cached update-check state with last-check time, current and available source identity, freshness, in-flight status, and actionable failure. Automatically refresh the remote at most once per hour by default, coalesce concurrent checks, and persist enough state across page refreshes and daemon restart. Do not run git fetch for every nav render, menu open, route change, SSE event, client poll, or reconnect. A manual check may request a fresh remote check, but duplicate clicks and concurrent clients must share one in-flight operation. In the web UI main navigation Controls menu, present one compact stateful control whenever the running Refine checkout/update channel is discoverable; do not gate the running Refine node's updater on whether the currently attached target app is itself Refine. When no update is known, the cached result is stale, or Refine is current, the control offers Check for updates and shows checking, current, stale, or error feedback as appropriate. When a newer fetched revision is available, the same control becomes an enabled Upgrade Refine button and identifies the available update without requiring the user to visit Refine (dev). During orchestration it shows durable progress, reconnecting, success, failure, and retry states. Preserve keyboard and screen-reader behavior. One click on Upgrade Refine is the authorization to begin; do not add a second confirmation dialog.

Clicking Upgrade Refine must launch exactly one dedicated managed upgrade Agent and return a durable operation receipt. The Agent owns the end-to-end maintenance plan and delegates privileged Git, process, installation, lifecycle, and source-promotion mutations through shared typed Refine capabilities rather than inventing browser-side shell commands. The operation must be idempotent across repeated clicks, browser closure, daemon termination, and restart, and must not consume a normal Goal workflow claim or deadlock by counting its own Agent or restart-safe handoff as upgrade-blocking active work.

Make workflow state an orchestration input rather than an affordance blocker. The Agent records the pre-upgrade pause/admission state, pauses new workflow claims when needed, observes active Goal agents, Quality, merge, build, terminal, and managed processes, and drains, checkpoints, or safely reconciles them before promotion. It must work when automation begins running, already paused, idle, or carrying active work. Preserve Goal records, claims, worktrees, branches, review boundaries, logs, and recoverable process state; never discard dirty work, force Git history, hide a failure, or report success from checkout HEAD alone. If a non-workflow source condition such as dirty or diverged controller source cannot be resolved safely and non-destructively, retain the checkout untouched and surface precise recovery evidence rather than forcing it.

Once safe, fetch and fast-forward the configured Refine source, build the candidate before stopping the live daemon, then use the existing restart-safe source-promotion and port-scoped service lifecycle machinery to activate and restart it. Prove success from the live daemon's candidate executable identity and health. On activation, registration, restart, reachability, or identity failure, use the existing authoritative rollback behavior and retain partial or unknown evidence plus actionable recovery; never claim the system is online while the wrong executable is running.

After restart, reconcile the same durable upgrade operation, restore the user's prior workflow admission intent rather than blindly resuming an intentionally paused workflow, recover or reconnect preserved workflow work and required managed infrastructure, and verify the Refine daemon, runner, attached target-app lifecycle, and UI event stream are online. The browser must automatically reconnect and settle the nav control from authoritative operation state. A completed update refreshes the cached source identity; a failed or interrupted update remains visible and safely retryable.

Extend the existing source-promotion, lifecycle, API, SSE, static/browser, and real installed-service tests where appropriate. Update the affected System/API/browser intent, Rust spec, and upgrade runbook so the manual Refine (dev) screen and the new Agent-orchestrated main-nav path have one shared authority and clearly documented recovery semantics. findings.description: The proposed authority remains ambiguous across operation JSON and source-promotion.json. Calling the registry authoritative and the latter repairable is insufficient without a single mutation API, monotonic revision, write order, and recovery rule for a crash between the two writes. The plan also omits migration behavior for Round 4 records that have an active handoff stage but no attempt, receipt, or claim fields. Finally, an 'unguessable' token cannot be treated as secret if persisted in projected progress, logs, or process command lines.
findings.recommendation: Put the complete handoff-attempt state and revision in the OperationHandle under the registry mutation lock; make source-promotion.json a derived projection rebuilt from that record after every mutation and at startup. Add serde-compatible schema/version defaults and explicitly settle legacy active records without correlated evidence as visible interrupted or failed states. Treat the token as a fencing nonce, or store only a verifier hash and redact the raw value from API/SSE/log/process projections.

findings.description: A structured receipt is not automatically liveness evidence. The current launcher returns no identity, detached launch discards the Child, and systemd/launchd submission success proves only manager acceptance. P3 does not define how each mechanism is queried and terminated, how detached PID reuse is excluded, or how startup avoids falsely settling zero claimants while a legitimately submitted helper is still starting. The crash after spawn but before parent receipt also means exactly-once process creation is not generally provable; the enforceable invariant is one attempt-owned claimant and one set of side effects.
findings.recommendation: Define a mechanism-specific receipt and observer interface: systemd unit plus invocation identity, launchd label/job identity, and detached PID plus start-time/executable/argument fingerprint. Persist submitted_at and an explicit bounded reconciliation deadline, require the helper to claim before sleep or mutation, and make named service-manager submission idempotent for the attempt. Specify exactly one authoritative claimant/side-effect owner, rejecting or terminating duplicate processes, rather than relying on an unprovable exactly-once spawn assertion.

findings.description: Cancellation is not wired through the actual shared surface. The current POST /operations/{id}/cancel path calls generic cancel_supervised, which only terminates managed processes; the restart-safe helper is intentionally external. P5's prose does not state how that route delegates to source-promotion ownership, so it can still publish cancelled while a helper mutates source or registration.
findings.recommendation: Add owner-aware capability cancellation behind the shared operation API. For source upgrades, durably fence cancellation first, reject later receipts/claims, query and terminate or await the exact external claimant, reconcile mutation stage, perform rollback and exact admission restoration, then settle the registry and projections. Exercise the real HTTP cancellation route at reservation, submitted, claimed, activation, rollback, and post-restart phases, including daemon restart during cancellation.

findings.description: P8 verifies only that Governance is configured, while the plan repeatedly relies on a specific Rule 4 handoff exception. findings.recommendation: Record the complete live Governance rule IDs and text before implementation and before completion, compare them with the pinned scenario's required semantics, and report any drift without editing Governance. Keep the pinned Latest Round authoritative for implementation, but do not claim current-Governance compliance from configured == true alone.
